decisions.rationale: Five consecutive gate FAILs. Run 5's verdict states most of its 14 findings were introduced or left half-landed by the remediation passes themselves. decisions.decision: 38-06's step-4a length table was corrected to 1175/1291/1298/1230 rather than reverting the four strings
decisions.rationale: Each test-file dismissal string grew by exactly 249 characters gaining a clause that records the analyser was inert when the comment was written. That is honest and prevents a future reader mistaking the dismissal for fresh-analysis-validated. The strings were right; the table was stale.

decisions.decision: Split PR #29 by reverting only two lines rather than dropping the whole pyproject.toml half
decisions.rationale: pyproject.toml carries the invariant that its pins mirror requirements.txt byte for byte; dropping it wholesale would have silently reverted 7 legitimate updates. Only fastapi and uvicorn[standard] are unsafe.

decisions.decision: Added dependabot ignore rules scoped by range, not by update-type
decisions.rationale: The FastAPI break regenerated three times (#21 to #25 to #29) because the weekly pip group had no ignore block. update-type scoping would not have blocked PR #34 at all, since starlette 0.40 to 1.6.0 is a MAJOR bump; a blanket ignore would suppress security advisories. starlette is held at >=0.46.0 only, the range fastapi 0.115.8 cannot satisfy.

uvicorn[standard] 0.30.6 requires websockets>=10.4 with no upper bound, so PR #35's >=17.1 resolves cleanly. The risk was untested rather than proven, and blocking on speculation is the wrong trade. CI passed on both runners.

decisions.decision: No PAT for this repo, ever
decisions.rationale: Public repo; an owner-identity token bypasses everything except the ruleset's deletion and non_fast_forward rules. A GitHub App is the right answer for release-please automation. Deferred alongside SCAN-08, because enforce_admins: true is what makes app-token automation safe to hold.

context_notes:
Phase 38 is planned, remediated across six passes, collapsed to one POSIX implementation, and committed. ZERO plans have executed and NO GitHub state has been mutated BY THE PHASE: no alert dismissed, no branch deleted, no protection changed, no workflow removed.

Master DID move a lot this session, but through ordinary PR merges outside the phase: nine PRs landed, the Dependabot queue went to zero, and release shoppybot-v2.1.0 was cut. That work is done and verified; it also made parts of Phase 38 redundant (38-02's cryptography task is now a no-op) and would have made another part actively harmful (38-03 and the runbook instructed preserving a v6/v7 divergence that, after #27/#28 merged, would have pinned the wheel job backwards and reverted two merged PRs).

The single most useful thing to carry forward is the method, not the state. Every real defect this phase has produced was found by MEASURING and none by reading. Reading missed the DI-04 fix landing in the plan but not the runbook across five passes; a byte-level diff caught it immediately. Reading `default-setup: state=configured` said code scanning was working; `languages: []` and `updated_at: null` said it was dead. Reading `rtk git status --porcelain` looked fine; measuring it showed it prints the 2-byte string `ok` on a clean tree, which made 38-01's dirty-tree gate permanently unsatisfiable. Guards were proven by stubbing the binary with fixture JSON and observing the mutation marker absent, not by inspecting the guard.

The collapse is the structural bet of this session. It removed the seam that produced runs 1 through 5 rather than fixing the fourteen symptoms one at a time. I would not claim gate run 6 passes; I would claim the specific failure mode no longer has a mechanism. If run 6 fails on NEW seams rather than the same ones, that is information worth having before executing anything irreversible.
